title.narrative: Individual measure 2021 - Action 3 - Democracy Support Alliance

description.narrative: Democracy is in decline. The world is experiencing a wave of `autocratisation¿ characterised by increasing executive power, erosion of democratic institutions, and a general constriction of fundamental freedoms. One-third of the world¿s population now live in countries undergoing autocratisation. The COVID-19 pandemic has only exacerbated this worrying trend.The urgency to adopt this project is related to the EU positioning ahead and towards the Summit for Democracy in the US (end of 2021). There is a 12-month window of opportunity to demonstrate the EU¿s leadership in a visible way, significantly influence the Summit¿s outcomes and ensure that we are ready to act, and not only react. The framing and content of the Summit are still in development, with countries expected to bring forward initiatives and make pledges. This action will help the EU and its Delegations to play an active role in defining and supporting short-term summit outcomes and their implementation immediately after the Summit.Democracy is essential for sustainable development. It increases economic growth, reduces inequalities, lowers rates of mortality and improves social outcomes. Nevertheless, democracy is often portrayed as a western invention; unfit and unnecessary for the wider world. The actions under this component would debunk such `myths¿, showcasing the advantages of democratic systems and promoting the best ways to support them, whatever the context. In the current context of political polarisation and social fracture, the need for (re)-building alliances on democracy and democracy support is all the greater. This requires a bold and inclusive `Team Europe¿ approach, including European Union (EU) Member States with different experiences and history, capable of developing a coalition beyond our borders, bringing in all states committed to building, protecting or improving their democracy. Based on the founding values of the EU, this action aims to: promote and protect democracy and human rights worldwide with actions based on academic evidence; share experiences on democracy support models; and build broad alliances to inform international and national policies, programmes and actions. It will work along three lines of action: (A) a `one stop shop¿ for democracy research and analysis, including on democracy support; (B) a structured operational network with Member States, sharing and pooling resources, helping develop conceptual and operational approaches for democracy support, and building coalitions with like-minded partners; (C) development of common EU and Member State outcomes and pilot actions ¿ where relevant, these should be related to the Biden Summit for Democracy. The network¿s first task would be to contribute to the Summit for Democracy and feed into the EU¿s positioning and preparations.
